findings.title: keychain_has's SEEN cache entries are never evicted for config_dirs that stop being queried
findings.detail: The static SEEN Vec only drops a config_dir's entry when keychain_has is called again for that same dir (the retain() call happens on the next lookup). If an account with a distinct configDir is removed, or a configDir is queried only once and then never again, its (PathBuf, Instant) entry is kept in the process-global Vec for the lifetime of the obid process, even though it immediately stops being 'fresh'. Over a long-running obid that adds/removes many Claude accounts with distinct configDirs over time, this is an unbounded, never-reclaimed growth (a slow memory leak), rather than a cache that naturally expires entries.

findings.title: Existing test/comment documents behavior this change silently reverses, with no new coverage added
findings.detail: This pre-existing test's comment says Cursor Keychain item presence is checked 'each time' a status is asked (only the token's value is throttled, to once a minute, via cursor_keychain_live). The diff now also caches the presence check itself (cursor_keychain_has) for LOOK_EVERY (2s) once an item is found, so three /v1/status calls made back-to-back here will perform the underlying 'security find-generic-password' existence probe only once instead of three times. The test doesn't assert on existence-probe counts (only on '-w' value-read counts), so it still passes, but the comment is now inaccurate and the diff ships its headline behavior change (status no longer asking security on every call) without any test asserting the new throttling actually happens for either keychain_has or cursor_keychain_has.
